A photographed live-action frame. Use reference image1 only for the same adult Korean woman’s face, black hair and bangs, earrings and blue-gray shirt; do not inherit its portrait crop or plain background. Natural skin and cloth at this distance, without reshaping, uniform pores or retouching.

Show its front corners, both receding side edges and the rear edge immediately in front of her torso so one continuous shared tabletop is unmistakable. A normal small cream ceramic cup, about9.5cm high and8cm across the rim, rests on the near-left part of this same table. The whole cup and handle are inside frame, with visible wood around the contact point. Its body is about half the height of Claire’s full visible head, not face-sized. Claire’s head, including the top of her hair, remains wholly inside the upper-right part of the frame. Her hands rest out of view.

A60mm lens look gives a medium view across the table, with the tabletop depth visible rather than filling the entire lower frame. Claire looks at the actual camera lens with relaxed closed lips. Focus sharply on the near cup rim and handle; Claire is softly defocused behind it while her identity and silhouette remain recognizable. One soft side window lights both subjects consistently. Quiet shelves behind her. No text, logos, steam, extra cups or oversized props.
video_prompt_common: One continuous six-second live-action shot starting at the supplied new photographic frame. Keep the normal cup scale, table geometry, contact point, face, camera framing, light and exposure unchanged. Claire keeps her gaze on the actual stationary camera lens with brief natural blinks and quiet nasal breathing; her head and chin keep the first-frame orientation, her lips relaxed, and she does not look down at the cup. The cup, chair and table remain still. The camera is physically locked, without push-in, zoom, cuts or scale changes. Native sound for this individual take: low workshop room tone and quiet breath across the full clip, without speech, music or a focus-motor effect.
